newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Dor in Polish petrol station venture.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Dor in Polish petrol station venture.

text.p: Israel's Dor Energy has signed a $400 million agreement with the state-owned Polish energy concern CPN to build 400 filling stations in Poland, Eli Hovav, managing director of Dor Energy Trading, said on Sunday.

Hovav said Dor, which is controlled by the Dankner Group, would hold 25 percent of the joint venture and CPN 50 percent. A third partner, which Hovav would only identify as a "foreign company," will hold the remaining 25 percent.

The three partners will invest proportionately in the new venture, which Hovav said planned to build the 400 filling stations over the next five years. Dor said the station would use the latest equipment and employ high service standards.
CPN has 1,300 filling stations of its own, which Dor said was about half the total in Poland today.
Hovav estimated that Dor, which is closely held, had sales of $500-600 million in 1996.

He said that in its domestic market, where the company supplies energy products to 150 filling stations in Israel and the Palestinian autonomous areas, the company was exploring developing ties with Texaco Inc, including possibly filling stations.
Last year, Dor and Caltex Oil Corp, a joint venture between Texaco and Chevron Corp, won a tender to supply jet fuel to airlines fueling in Israel equal to 40 percent of the total market.
Hovav estimated the tender was worth $50-60 million.
